name: International Rescue Committee
mission: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic well being, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is at work in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities.
theoryOfChange: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) utilizes an "Outcomes and Evidence Framework" (OEF) and an "interactive Outcomes and Evidence Framework (iOEF)" as a set of tools to guide practitioners in designing effective program activities and models. This framework includes defined outcome areas and explicit theories of change that articulate the necessary steps to achieve specific outcomes. The IRC systematically uses theories of change in all new project designs to ensure they are outcome-driven and evidence-based. The organization focuses on five outcome areas: Health, Safety, Education, Economic Wellbeing, and Power, with 17 outcomes, each having a gender-sensitive theory of change. Additionally, the IRC has an "IMPACT Framework" which is its Crisis Response, Recovery and Development Department's Program Quality Framework, applying to all Country Programs to advance high-quality programming.

With a <cite id="15">board of 35 members</cite> and a <cite id="16">97% independent board rate</cite>, the organization maintains rigorous oversight. rich_narrative.summary: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is a global humanitarian powerhouse that has been helping people survive and rebuild their lives since its <cite id="1">founding in 1933</cite>. Operating in over 40 countries, the organization focuses on health, education, and economic wellbeing for those displaced by conflict and natural disasters. In FY2024, the IRC demonstrated significant scale by managing <cite id="2">$1,529,582,620 in total revenue</cite>, reflecting a <cite id="3">3-year revenue growth rate of 5.5%</cite>. The organization is particularly efficient at converting donor dollars into direct aid. It maintains a <cite id="4">program expense ratio of 87.7%</cite> according to its latest filings, which significantly <cite id="5">beats the 75% industry standard</cite> for humanitarian groups. Furthermore, the IRC is highly effective at fundraising, spending only <cite id="6">$0.06 to raise every $1</cite>. For Muslim donors, the IRC offers a specialized <cite id="7">Zakat-eligible fund</cite> that directs 100% of applicable donations to eligible categories like <cite id="8">the poor (fuqara) and needy (masakin)</cite>. While the organization operates with a lean <cite id="9">2.4 months of working capital</cite>, its massive reach and <cite id="10">perfect 100/100 scores in Culture and Leadership</cite> from Charity Navigator signal a highly stable and professional institution.
